concepts.def: Rutherford alpha scattering proved tiny dense nucleus

walkthroughs.body_html:
Models evolved as new evidence appeared.

Thomson: plum pudding. Rutherford fired alpha particles at gold foil - most went through, some bounced back.

This proved a small dense nucleus. Bohr later added shells; Chadwick discovered neutrons.

Li, Na, K all react with water to make a hydroxide + hydrogen.

Reactivity increases down the group: outer electron is further from the nucleus, easier to lose.

Potassium gives a lilac flame; sodium fizzes vigorously.

F, Cl, Br, I exist as diatomic molecules like Cl2.

Reactivity decreases down: outer shell further from nucleus, harder to gain an electron.

A more reactive halogen displaces a less reactive one from its salt.

mcqs.q: Rutherford's gold foil experiment showed atoms have:
Which is most reactive: Li, Na, K or Rb?
Why does first ionisation energy generally increase across a period?
options: Atoms across a period have more shells, pulling electrons closer.
Atoms get bigger across a period, making electrons easier to add but harder to remove.
Nuclear charge increases while shielding stays roughly constant, so electrons are held more tightly.
Mass is spread evenly throughout the entire atom including the electron shells.

mcqs.q: Where is almost all the mass of an atom located?
options: Mass is spread evenly throughout the entire atom including the electron shells.
In the nucleus, made up of protons and neutrons.
Electrons contribute significantly to the mass of an atom.
Atoms across a period have more shells, pulling electrons closer.

mcqs.q: What is different between two isotopes of the same element?
options: Atoms across a period have more shells, pulling electrons closer.
Isotopes are atoms of different elements with the same mass.
They have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.
Isotopes have different numbers of electrons, which is why their mass differs.
